reasoning.title: Open the repository’s commit history
reasoning.description: Use this when a GitLab task asks about individual commits by date or author; do not rely on the project’s total commit count, Contributors page, activity feed, or other aggregate reports.
reasoning.content: From the project, expand “Repository” and select “Commits,” then choose the relevant branch and use the available date navigation or filters. Continue through pagination or “Load more” until the entire requested date range is visible; aggregate pages cannot establish which specific commits qualify.

reasoning.title: Enumerate and verify every qualifying commit
reasoning.description: Use this for counts constrained by a date and one or more authors, especially when several commits share a date or displayed identities are similar; it is unnecessary only when the requested value is already explicitly shown as a complete filtered total.
reasoning.content: Inspect every row in the requested date group, match each displayed author exactly, and count all qualifying rows across every named person rather than guessing from the question. Open a commit’s detail view if the list abbreviates the author or date, distinguish near-identical identities, and answer only after the qualifying commits and final count are visibly verified.

reasoning.title: Open the branch commit history
reasoning.description: Use when counting commits by author and date within a project; do not rely on the overview or the aggregate “Contributors” report, which may not support date-specific filtering.
reasoning.content: In project navigation, expand “Repository” and select “Commits,” then confirm the correct branch or tag in the branch selector. Locate the requested date group using available filters or by scrolling and pagination; do not answer while only the navigation sidebar is visible.

reasoning.title: Count every visibly matching commit
reasoning.description: Use after the commit list has reached the requested date, especially when multiple authors, pagination, or abbreviated identities are involved; not for merely confirming that the commits page exists.
reasoning.content: Enumerate every commit whose displayed date and author exactly match the requested criteria, continuing through all rows and any next page or load-more control for that date. Open a commit detail when an author name is abbreviated, distinguish near-identical identities, and sum the per-author counts only from entries visibly verified on GitLab.

reasoning.title: Locate the project with global search
reasoning.description: Use when the dashboard’s “Filter by name” shows no match; that filter only narrows projects already listed on the dashboard, whereas “Search GitLab” searches across the site.
reasoning.content: Enter the project name in “Search GitLab,” submit the search, verify the namespace and exact project-name variant in the results, then open the matching project. Do not treat an empty dashboard filter as proof that the project does not exist.

reasoning.title: Read the SSH value from the Clone menu
reasoning.description: Use when asked for an SSH clone URL or command from a project page; do not use the browser URL, an SSH-key warning, or a presumed GitLab host/port as substitutes.
reasoning.content: Open the visible “Clone” control and wait until its menu or popover is observable, then select or read the SSH—not HTTPS—entry and copy the complete displayed value, including scheme or user, host, port if shown, namespace, repository path, and suffix. Only prepend `git clone` if the menu displays a URL rather than a full command, and do not answer until the exact SSH value is visibly verified.

reasoning.title: Locate and verify the project
reasoning.description: Use when opening a GitLab project by name, especially if the dashboard project filter is empty or stale; do not rely on results from the wrong project scope.
reasoning.content: Select the visible “All” project scope before entering the name in “Filter by name,” because changing scope can reset the filter. If results remain stale, use the global “Search GitLab” searchbox, open the project result, and verify its full namespace and project name to avoid a near-identical repository.

reasoning.title: Ground the SSH clone command
reasoning.description: Use when asked for an SSH clone URL or command from a GitLab project; do not infer it from the browser URL, repository path, or HTTPS variant.
reasoning.content: On the project page, open the visible “Clone” control and capture a fresh observation that includes the complete “Clone with SSH” value, scrolling or expanding the menu if the snapshot is truncated. Copy the entire displayed value exactly, verify the SSH entry rather than the HTTPS look-alike, and prepend `git clone ` only when a command is requested; never answer unless the full value is visibly grounded.

reasoning.title: Locate the exact project reliably
reasoning.description: Use when opening a repository by name, especially when the dashboard’s project filter returns no results under a limited scope; do not assume an empty Personal view means the project is unavailable.
reasoning.content: Switch the project list to “All” and reapply “Filter by name”; if it remains empty, use the header “Search GitLab,” submit the query, and open the matching project result. Confirm the full namespace and project name in the result or project breadcrumbs to avoid near-identical repositories.

reasoning.title: Capture the displayed SSH clone value
reasoning.description: Use when asked for an SSH clone command from a project page; this does not apply when another protocol such as HTTPS is explicitly requested.
reasoning.content: Open the visible “Clone” control and wait until the expanded menu is present in a fresh page observation. Copy the complete value labeled “Clone with SSH” exactly—including scheme, host, port if shown, namespace, project path, and suffix—then prepend `git clone `; never infer it from the browser URL or report it unless the full value is visibly captured.

reasoning.title: Verify project ranking in Search
reasoning.description: Use when selecting the best GitLab project by language or project metrics; do not use an autocomplete suggestion or a truncated result preview as proof of rank.
reasoning.content: Enter the query in the visible “Search GitLab” searchbox, submit it, open the “Projects” results, and apply the relevant language and sort controls if available. Inspect the complete metric values for every qualifying row, open details when names or values are abbreviated, and report every tie; never call the first visible result “best” unless the displayed ordering and metrics prove it.

reasoning.title: Read the SSH value from Clone
reasoning.description: Use after opening the chosen project when an SSH clone command is requested; the project path, browser URL, or an SSH-key warning is not a substitute for the displayed clone URL.
reasoning.content: On the project repository page, expand the visible “Clone” control and locate the option explicitly labeled for SSH. Copy the full displayed SSH value exactly, verify it appears in the captured page content, and only then prefix it with `git clone `; if the menu or value is not visible, reopen it or use its copy control and verify the copied text rather than reconstructing the URL.

reasoning.title: Search and rank all project results
reasoning.description: Use when identifying the most-starred GitLab project matching a description; do not rely on an exact-phrase search that returns no projects or on a partial first page.
reasoning.content: Start with the global “Search GitLab” field, submit the query, select or verify the “Projects” result type, and broaden the terms if necessary. Review every result page, confirm each candidate from its name and description, record the visibly displayed star count for every qualifying project, and include all ties rather than inferring a winner from truncated results.

reasoning.title: Extract the visible SSH clone command
reasoning.description: Use after the winning project has been verifiably identified; not when only a narrated claim, abbreviated grid value, or hidden menu is available.
reasoning.content: Open the project, activate the visible “Clone” control, and read the complete value labeled “Clone with SSH”; do not confuse it with “Clone with HTTPS” or reconstruct it from the browser URL. Ensure the full SSH value is present in the captured page output, then copy it exactly and prepend `git clone ` only if the task requests a command.

reasoning.title: Use the project’s branch commit history
reasoning.description: Apply when counting commits by author over a date interval; do not use “Contributors” when an exact branch-and-date-filtered count is required.
reasoning.content: Open “Repository” → “Commits,” select the intended branch, and navigate the history using its date or pagination controls rather than relying on repeated wheel scrolling. If using the repository commits API, call the API on the same GitLab host as the project and preserve the exact namespace; switching to the public GitLab host can produce a misleading “Project Not Found” response.

reasoning.title: Bound and enumerate the complete interval
reasoning.description: Apply once the commit history or API results are visible; do not answer from a partially inspected month, a single page, or a provisional subtotal.
reasoning.content: Inspect every page until rows are visibly bounded on both sides of the requested interval, counting every qualifying commit exactly once and checking the full author name in the commit detail when the list is abbreviated or ambiguous. For API results, request successive pages until no more records remain, verify each displayed timestamp and author against the inclusive boundaries, and only then report the total.

reasoning.title: Use the instance’s commit history and valid filters
reasoning.description: Use when counting commits by author within a date range in a GitLab project; do not substitute the Contributors report, which aggregates activity and may not support the required date/status filtering.
reasoning.content: Open Repository → Commits (or the project’s visible “Commits” link), select the correct branch, and use the visible “Author” control only if its autocomplete produces a selectable account—typed text or Enter alone does not apply the filter. If the UI truncates results, query the same GitLab instance’s repository commits API with the project path URL-encoded, branch, date bounds, and pagination; do not switch to the public GitLab host unless the project actually lives there.

reasoning.title: Prove complete coverage before counting
reasoning.description: Use when commit rows are paginated, lazily loaded, accessibility output is truncated, or an author name has close variants; not when the requested result is already a single fully displayed aggregate.
reasoning.content: Enumerate every returned page or every chronological row from the upper boundary through the lower boundary, stopping only after a row outside the range is visible, and count all qualifying rows including ties or multiple commits on one date. Verify the full author identity and date on each row—open the commit detail if the list abbreviates the name—and never infer unseen rows or treat a partial range as a zero count.

reasoning.title: Stay on the project’s Commits page
reasoning.description: Use when counting a person’s commits in a GitLab project; do not switch to the public GitLab domain or rely on Contributors analytics when exact dated history is required.
reasoning.content: Open Repository → Commits, expand the visible “Author” control, search for the person, and select an actual matching option before proceeding. Confirm the selected author is shown as an active filter; if no option appears, inspect commits on the current site rather than constructing a cross-domain URL that may trigger verification.

reasoning.title: Count the complete filtered date range
reasoning.description: Use after reaching the commit history for an author and time period; do not infer a count from a partial page, grouped heading, or abbreviated identity.
reasoning.content: Traverse every results page or load-more section covering the target period, count every qualifying commit row, and stop only after crossing both date boundaries. Verify each row’s full author identity and date—opening commit details when text is abbreviated—and keep near-identical author variants separate unless the displayed details prove they are the same person.

reasoning.title: Use the dedicated Contributors report
reasoning.description: When locating contributor commit rankings for a repository; not when aggregate repository activity or delivery metrics are requested.
reasoning.content: From Projects, use “Explore” and its “Filter by name” field if the project is not in “Yours,” open the exact namespace/project match, then expand “Repository” and select “Contributors.” Do not substitute “Analytics” or “Repository Analytics,” which can show aggregate author statistics without the contributor ranking.

reasoning.title: Verify and extract the ranked rows
reasoning.description: After the “Contributors” page opens and the task asks for ranked names and commit totals.
reasoning.content: Wait for contributor data to render, then scroll through and inspect the actual rows or cards until each reported full name and commit count is visibly confirmed; open details if a displayed identity is abbreviated, and distinguish near-identical identities. Return exactly the requested rank positions, while explicitly including every row tied at a qualifying boundary, and never infer values from an uninspected page.

reasoning.title: Open the project Members page
reasoning.description: Use when identifying everyone with access to a GitLab project; do not rely on Activity, repository pages, or a group-level members page when the request is project-specific.
reasoning.content: From the project sidebar, expand “Project information” and select “Members.” Confirm the page title and breadcrumbs identify the intended project before reading access entries.

reasoning.title: Inspect and enumerate the complete member list
reasoning.description: Use for exhaustive requests such as “who else” or “everyone with access,” especially when GitLab may show direct, inherited, invited-group, paginated, or off-screen entries.
reasoning.content: Read every member row and section, scrolling and advancing pagination or expanding hidden results until the list is exhausted; exclude the signed-in requester only when “else” requires it. Copy each username exactly as visibly displayed, opening the profile/detail view if the row truncates it, and never infer a username from a display name or report one that was not observed.

reasoning.title: Verify the branch with visible search results
reasoning.description: Use when a GitLab task requests contributor statistics for a specific branch; do not use the currently selected branch or an unchanged picker row as proof that the requested branch is absent.
reasoning.content: Open Repository → Contributors, use the branch selector, and confirm that its label changes to the requested branch before reading rankings. If the picker is inconclusive, open Repository → Branches → All, enter the exact branch name, activate Search, and inspect the resulting rows or explicit empty-state message; the selector may continue showing the selected branch while filtering, which is a look-alike trap rather than a matching result.

reasoning.title: Extract every top contributor’s full email from evidence
reasoning.description: Use after the Contributors report is visibly filtered to the requested branch; do not answer from an unfiltered report, a guessed identity, or an abbreviated grid value.
reasoning.content: Read the complete ranking and include every contributor tied for the highest commit count. For each qualifying row, open the contributor or a corresponding commit detail if necessary and copy the full displayed author email exactly, verifying near-identical names and addresses rather than inferring the email from the name.

reasoning.title: Preserve the exact branch target
reasoning.description: Use when a GitLab task requests branch-specific repository data; do not apply default-branch results when the named branch cannot be confirmed.
reasoning.content: Open Repository → Branches, select the visible “All” tab, search the exact branch name, and then select that exact revision in the branch selector before opening Repository → Contributors. Confirm the page title, breadcrumb, or URL still names the requested branch; if it does not exist or cannot be selected, report that limitation rather than substituting the default branch.

reasoning.title: Read and verify the complete contributor ranking
reasoning.description: Use after reaching the Contributors report for the verified branch; do not answer from an unrendered chart, a guessed ordering, or values seen only on another branch.
reasoning.content: Wait for the contributor rows or chart labels to render, then copy the full displayed commit count from the highest-ranked row and inspect all equally ranked rows for ties. Ensure every reported value is visibly present in the page observations, and distinguish commit counts from additions, deletions, issue badges, or other nearby numbers; open a detail view if a label or value is abbreviated.
